Small to medium, with a profilefunctions unit test in the pattern of tests/profile-switch-preprocessing.test.js. (Superseded by the fix below, which applies timeshift the way AndroidAPS 3.x does.)

Fixed 2026-09-25 on local branch bf/profile-switch-percentage 5a895b49 (one commit on origin/dev e3adc91d, not pushed; worktree externals/work/crm-6a-fix-profile-switch-percentage). A switch of the AndroidAPS 3.x shape (an embedded profileJson, a numeric percentage, timeshift in milliseconds, no CircadianPercentageProfile) is read as AndroidAPS reads it: basal × pct/100, ISF and carb ratio × 100/pct, targets and DIA unscaled, and every schedule looked up at t − (timeshift truncated to whole hours), wrapped to one day (AndroidAPS 7e1d537d49, BlockExtension.kt:14-18, ProfileSealed.kt:77, :324-365). Requests for a named profile are not adjusted. The probe exits 1 on e3adc91d and 0 on the branch; 35 new tests (tests/profile-switch-percentage.test.js); full suite 3205/0/3 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43). Not checked in a browser (the chart's basal line, the reports).

Left for the maintainer: the CircadianPercentageProfile path, which is unchanged. Its intended timeshift direction (t + offset, AAPS 2.x) is the opposite of AAPS 3.x's (reversed in AndroidAPS 37e3c4532a), and, as measured above, it never applies the shift anyway. Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): leave it as it is; it is not a defect to fix.

docs.title: BF-124 · the treatment tooltip converts a BG that is already in display units
docs.text:
Mechanism. Treatments with carbs, insulin, protein or fat are drawn by renderer.drawTreatment, whose mouseover handler is treatmentTooltip inside appendTreatments (lib/client/renderer.js:638-645 on v15.0.8 92d08342, :641-648 on dev 4f705217). It starts from treatment.glucose and, when client.settings.units != client.ddata.profile.getUnits(), multiplies by 1/18 (display mmol) or 18 (display mg/dL). The record's own units field is not consulted, so the conversion is right only when the record happens to be in the profile's units. The careportal saves a BG with units: client.settings.units, the display units (lib/client/careportal.js:321, gatherData), so an entered BG is converted a second time exactly when display and profile units differ. BG Check records (no carbs or insulin) are drawn by addTreatmentCircles, whose tooltip prints d.glucose as stored, which matches the report's observation that BG Check entries look right. The report's two affected sites being the ones fed by Loop is consistent with an mg/dL profile under an mmol/L display (read-derived; the sites were not examined).

Reproduced 2026-09-25 with tools/lab/triage-2026-09/tooltip-bg-units.js, which draws a Meal Bolus (10 g carbs, a BG) with the tree's own renderer.drawTreatment in a jsdom document (the tree's tests/fixtures/secure-jsdom.js and dom-globals.js, as tests/stored-output-sinks.test.js does for this tooltip), dispatches mouseover and reads the "BG:" value. d3 comes from the tree: 5.16.0 for v15.0.8 (its own lockfile's node_modules), 7.9.0 for dev. Identical results on both:

case display profile stored tooltip BG arm mmol mg/dl 5 mmol 0.3 (want 5) arm mg/dl mmol 90 mg/dl 1621 (want 90) arm mmol mmol 90 mg/dl 90 (want 5) control mmol mmol 5 mmol 5 control mg/dl mg/dl 90 mg/dl 90 control, converted mmol mg/dl 90 mg/dl 5 control, BG Check dot mmol mg/dl 5 mmol 5

Break-it check: on a scratch copy of dev 4f705217 where the tooltip converts from treatment.units (falling back to the profile's units when a record has none), the three arms show 5, 90 and 5, the controls are unchanged, and the probe exits 0.

Not run: a real browser, the chart position of the bubble (the triage reading is that it is correct; not measured), the day-to-day and treatments reports, and a survey of which uploaders write units on treatments other than the careportal.

Fix shape (measured on a scratch copy only): in treatmentTooltip, take the source units from treatment.units when present (normalising mmol/mmol/L and mg/dl/mg/dL), else from the profile, and convert only when they differ from the display units. Add a jsdom test beside the existing tooltip test in tests/stored-output-sinks.test.js or in tests/client.renderer.test.js.

docs.title: BF-125 · IFTTT Maker events use translated level names; a failed call re-sends the alarm every check
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8773 (merge e759a989, head 54bf05d2); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Half 1, the event name. lib/server/pushnotify.js sendMakerEvent (:124-144) builds the event with level: levels.toLowerCase(notify.level) (:131). lib/levels.js toLowerCase returns toDisplay(level).toLowerCase(), and toDisplay runs the English label through levels.translate (:17-37), which lib/server/bootevent.js points at the site's language (:218 on v15.0.8, :247 on dev). lib/plugins/maker.js makeRequests (:82-97) then triggers ns-event, ns-<level> and ns-<level>-<plugin>. Node percent-encodes the non-ASCII path, so the request is sent, but with an event name no applet written from the documentation listens for.

Half 2, the resend. emitNotification stores the alarm's dedup key with a 30-second TTL before sending (:50). Only the success callbacks of the Pushover send (:100) and of the Maker send (:141) extend it to 15 minutes. maker.makeKeyRequest reports an error only when the HTTPS request itself errors (any HTTP response counts as success), and async.series stops at the first error. So when a Maker call errors, and Pushover is not configured, the key expires after 30 s and the same alarm goes out again at the next evaluation: the "every minute" in the report. The reporter's log shows ns-event sent and no ns-<translated> line, consistent with the second call failing; what made it fail there (their Node version, or IFTTT's answer to a non-ASCII event name) is not established.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 with tools/lab/triage-2026-09/maker-language.js, which wires lib/language, lib/levels, lib/plugins/maker and lib/server/pushnotify the way bootevent.js does and emits a WARN alarm from simplealarms. Nothing reaches IFTTT: https.get is replaced by an http.get of the same URL to a stub on 127.0.0.1, which records the event name. Identical on v15.0.8 (its own lockfile's node_modules) and dev 4f705217:

arm triggers en (control) ns-event, ns-warning, ns-warning-simplealarms ru ns-event, ns-осторожно, ns-осторожно-simplealarms de ns-event, ns-warnung, ns-warnung-simplealarms resend arm (same alarm at t = 0 / 45 s / 16 min) triggers sent stub answers 200, en (control) 3 / 0 / 3 stub answers 200, ru 3 / 0 / 3 stub resets the connection, en 1 / 1 / 1

Language count: on v15.0.8, 28 of the 29 non-English languages translate "Warning" or "Urgent" (Slovenian cannot be loaded there, its file name is wrong; fixed on dev by 470365b2); on dev, 30 of 30. Break-it check: on a scratch copy of dev 4f705217 with the event level taken from an untranslated map, ru and de give ns-warning and the probe exits 0.

Not run: a real IFTTT call, Pushover, older Node versions (the engines field is >=20), and a booted server.

Fix shape (half 1 measured on a scratch copy only): name Maker events from an untranslated level key (urgent, warning, info, …) and keep the translated label only in value1/value2. For half 2, decide whether a failed Maker call should hold the key for longer than 30 s (for example, the snooze period), so a failing integration does not re-send every check; tests/pushnotify.test.js with language.set('ru') is the pattern. Sites that renamed their applets to the translated event names would need a release note.

Half 1 fixed 2026-09-25 on local branch bf/maker-level-names 2f50ada9 (one commit on origin/dev e3adc91d, not pushed; worktree externals/work/crm-6a-fix-maker-level-names). A new levels.toKey returns the untranslated lower-case level (urgent, warning, info, low, lowest, none, unknown), and sendMakerEvent names the event from it, so en, ru and de sites send identical event names; value1/value2 keep the translated title and message. The probe exits 1 on e3adc91d and 0 on the branch. 11 new tests (tests/maker-level-names.test.js); full suite 3181/0/3 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43).

Half 2 kept by decision. The 2015 commits f805633f and ea745065 say a failed send is retried, which is what the 30-second key does. The branch's tests now pin that behaviour (a failing stub is retried), so a change to it is a visible decision. Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): keep it. A failed Maker call keeps being retried about every 30 s, so the entry is recorded fixed. With more than one Maker key, the retry does not cover a key that fails while another succeeds (BF-137).

Release note needed. A site that renamed its IFTTT applets to the translated event names must rename them back to ns-warning, ns-urgent and ns-<level>-<plugin>.

docs.title: BF-126 · a nameless authorization subject ends the server at every boot
docs.text:
Mechanism. Authorization subjects live in the auth_subjects collection. After any subject write, and once during boot (setupAuthorization), storage.reload() lists the subjects and, when API_SECRET is set, derives each one's access token: a prefix built from subject.name.toLowerCase() and a digest of its _id. Nothing on the write path requires a name: storage.createSubject stores the body it is given (on dev, after #8754, only the fields in SUBJECT_FIELDS — name, roles, notes, created_at — but none is required). For a row without name, the token derivation throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase'). The throw happens inside the MongoDB driver's callback, where nothing catches it, so the process exits. Every later boot reads the same row in the same place and exits the same way. The admin page is not the path: its form sends the input's value, which is always a string (lib/admin_plugins/subjects.js:121, read).

Lines: v15.0.8 92d08342 — lib/authorization/storage.js reload :161, throw at :190, createSubject :130; lib/authorization/endpoints.js :44. dev 4f705217 — storage.js reload :220, throw at :256, createSubject :189, SUBJECT_FIELDS :51; endpoints.js :48.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 with a probe held outside this repository (the defect is live on 15.0.8), which boots the tree's lib/server/server.js against a fresh MongoDB 7 database (random API_SECRET, AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied, bound to 127.0.0.1) and authenticates as admin. On both v15.0.8 (its own lockfile's node_modules) and dev 4f705217:

step v15.0.8 dev 4f705217 server answers /api/v1/status.json 200 200 control: create a subject with a name, then status 3 s later 200, 200 200, 200 create a subject without a name connection reset; process exit code 1; TypeError … 'toLowerCase' at storage.js:190 same, at storage.js:256 nameless rows in auth_subjects 1 1 restart on the same database no 200 within 30 s; exit code 1, same TypeError same remove the row in MongoDB, restart 200 200

The last row is the liveness check: the probe tells a dead server from a live one in the same run. Break-it check: on a scratch copy of dev 4f705217 with the token prefix computed from String(subject.name || ''), the same request answers 200 and the server stays up (probe exit 0).

Not run: a role without a name (the roles list is sorted with a.name.localeCompare at :180 / :239, which would throw the same way; read-derived), a subject whose name is not a string (also read-derived), and hosting platforms' restart behaviour (the outage lasts until the row is removed however often the platform restarts the process).

Fix shape (not measured beyond the one-line guard above): refuse a subject or role without a non-empty string name in create() and save() with a 400, and make reload() skip and log a malformed row instead of throwing, so an existing bad row cannot keep a site down. tests/authsubjects.test.js is the pattern for the test.

docs.title: BF-127 · clock views opened from the menu are blank for a token viewer on a denied site
docs.text:
A viewer given a token link (/?token=<subject token>) reads the main page because lib/client/index.js takes the token from the page address (browserUtils.queryParms().token) and uses it for /api/v1/status.json and an authorization request. The token stays in the address and in memory (client.authorized). It is not written to storage.

The Clock menu (views/index.html:175-179) links to /clock/<face> with no query string, and nothing in lib/client/ rewrites those links (git grep -E "clockcolorlink|bgclocklink|clocklink" origin/dev -- lib/client finds nothing). The clock page then:

  1. Loads /api/v1/status.js, with ?secret= if localStorage holds apisecrethash, or ?token= from its own address (views/clockviews/clock.html:36-56). Otherwise it sends no credentials. client.init() runs only in that script's onload (clock.html:59-61), and there is no onerror handler.
  2. Fetches /api/v2/properties the same way (lib/client/clock-client.js:35-63). A failed fetch only logs (see the #7036 entry), so nothing is ever drawn.

On a denied site a page opened from the menu has no credentials, so step 1 is refused. The script's onload does not fire for a 401, so the clock never starts (read: browser script-loading behaviour, not run in a browser). Even if it did, step 2 would be refused, and the probe measures that step. A viewer who signed in with the API secret is not affected, because the secret hash is in localStorage, which the clock reads.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 by tools/lab/triage-2026-09/clock-token-link.js:

  • Server arm. Two servers were booted, one per tree, against a fresh MongoDB 7.0 container. Settings: AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied, ENABLE=careportal, a random API secret. On each, a subject with the readable role was created and one reading was posted. Results, identical on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev 4f705217:
request no token with the subject's token GET /clock/clock-color 200 200 GET /api/v1/status.js 401 200 GET /api/v2/properties 401 200 (the reading)

The main page /?token=… served on both trees carries the four clock links as plain paths.

  • Client arm. This runs the shipping clock-client.js in the tree's jsdom fixture, with $.ajax stubbed as a denied site: success only when the URL carries the token, and a 401 error otherwise. The page URL is taken from the tree's own views/index.html menu link. The arm tested is the page at /clock/clock-color: one request with no token, and nothing drawn (.sg empty, #inner has no children). The control is the page at /clock/clock-color?token=…: one request with the token, and the value drawn (120). Both trees exit 1.

The token used was generated for the run in a throwaway database, was never printed, and was deleted with the container.

Not run: a real browser, so step 1's onload behaviour for a 401 is read, not measured. Also not run: the /clock/config face, and a site with AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=readable, where the clock needs no token and works.

Fix shape (not measured): carry the token that opened the main page into the clock links, for example by appending the current token query parameter to the #…clocklink hrefs when the menu is built. A second option is for the clock to use the same credential the main page resolved. Either way, give the clock a visible message when its fetch is refused. It is small, with a client test in the tests/clock-client.test.js pattern. Whether a token should be copied into further URLs (and so into history and referrers) is a maintainer decision. The token is already in the main page's own URL.

docs.title: BF-128 · /pebble?units=mgdl on an mmol site returns the delta in mmol
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8777 (merge d613c35f, head 4864d679); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Mechanism. In lib/server/pebble.js (identical on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev 4f705217) the route's middleware sets req.mmol = (req.query.units || env.settings.units) === 'mmol' (:177). The reading is scaled from req.mmol (mapSGVs, :35-59), so ?units=mgdl gives mg/dL. The delta comes from the bgnow plugin's delta.scaled, which is scaled by the sandbox's settings.units (lib/plugins/bgnow.js:171). prepareSandbox (:143-154) copies the site's settings and sets units = 'mmol' when req.mmol is true (:146-148), but leaves the site's units in place otherwise. On an mmol/L site (DISPLAY_UNITS containing "mmol", normalised to mmol by lib/server/env.js:201-202) asking for mg/dL, the delta stays in mmol/L, and because req.mmol is false it is not passed through toFixed(1) either, so it is a bare number.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 with tools/lab/triage-2026-09/pebble-units.js, which runs the tree's own pebble middleware and handler in-process with a ctx built the way bootevent.js builds it (language, levels, the server plugin registry) and two readings 5 minutes apart, 92 then 90 mg/dL. Identical on v15.0.8 (its own lockfile's node_modules) and dev 4f705217:

case sgv bgdelta arm: mmol site, ?units=mgdl "90" -0.1 (want -2) control: mmol site, no units "5.0" "-0.1" control: mg/dL site, ?units=mmol "5.0" "-0.1" control: mg/dL site, no units "90" -2

Break-it check: on a scratch copy of dev 4f705217 with prepareSandbox setting the units in both directions, the arm gives sgv "90", bgdelta -2 and the probe exits 0.

Not run: a booted server (authorization and the HTTP layer were not exercised; the probe calls the middleware and handler directly), tests/pebble.test.js (it boots against MongoDB), and any watch face. The IOB/BWP/COB fields /pebble adds were not checked for the same mismatch.

Clients (read). No client in the corpora under externals/ calls Nightscout's /pebble; xDrip serves its own /pebble locally (externals/xDrip/app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/webservices/WebServicePebble.java, read). The callers are watch faces and similar outside the corpora, so how many sites are affected is unknown. A past maintainer comment on the issue suggested deprecating the endpoint.

Fix shape first written here, now known to be unsafe: in prepareSandbox, set clonedEnv.settings.units = req.mmol ? 'mmol' : 'mg/dl'. It fixes the delta, but the Bolus Wizard Preview fields /pebble adds then compare a mg/dL reading with the site's mmol/L profile: on an mmol/L site asked for mg/dL it gives bwp "20.32" where the site's own value is "-0.96" (measured 2026-09-25). Do not use it.

Fixed 2026-09-25 on local branch bf/pebble-delta-units aa224c69 (one commit on origin/dev e3adc91d, not pushed; worktree externals/work/crm-6a-fix-pebble-delta-units). addDelta takes delta.mgdl unless mmol is requested, and delta.scaled (mmol, as before) when it is. The sandbox units are not changed, so bwp, bwpo, iob and cob are computed exactly as before. The probe exits 1 on e3adc91d and 0 on the branch. 21 new tests (tests/pebble-units.test.js: site mg/dL or mmol × no units, ?units=mgdl, ?units=mmol × rising, falling, flat; the legacy 0 with no delta; the BWP, IOB and COB fields unchanged by ?units on an mmol site); full suite 3191/0/3 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43).

Filed 2026-09-26. Two further observations from the fix are now entries of their own:

  • BF-138: on an mg/dL site asked for ?units=mmol, /pebble computes the Bolus Wizard Preview in an mmol sandbox against the mg/dL profile (bwp -2.17 where the site's own value is -0.96). aa224c69 does not change this.
  • BF-139: a shared-state mechanism, in which the values one /pebble request scales can persist on data shared with later requests. Mechanism only.

Maintainer decision 2026-09-26: both are fixed in 15.0.9 on this branch, in one PR with BF-128. Both are fixed on the branch (b58b937c BF-139, then b3db0f36 BF-138; see their sections). One of aa224c69's tests expected bwpo to be unchanged by ?units on an mmol site; with BF-138's fix bwpo follows ?units=mgdl, so that expectation was changed by design. Suite on b3db0f36 3216/0/3.

docs.title: BF-132 · on #8730, the Crowdin sync reverts translations dev corrected
8730 (crowdin_incoming, head f99c0e54, opened 2026-09-21 by the Crowdin integration) carries
docs.text:
Crowdin's current strings. Dev's 9f249815 corrected several of them in the repository, and Crowdin was not updated, so merging #8730 puts the older strings back.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 in the release-candidate pre-flight (dev ecb63223 + #8758 and its fixes + #8568 + #8419 + #8730, tree dd51bb8a): four tests in tests/language.test.js fail in all six Node × MongoDB cells and pass on dev: expected '克' to be '毫升' (zh_TW "ml"), expected '碳水' to be '碳水化合物' (zh_TW "Carbs"), expected 'Days with food' to be 'Dagar med mat' (sv_SE), and the Russian status-line substitution. Read from the files: git show refs/triage/pr-8730:translations/zh_TW.json has "ml": "克"; dev has "毫升".

Fix shape (not measured): correct the strings in Crowdin to match dev, then let Crowdin refresh #8730, or close it and take the next sync. A commit pushed to crowdin_incoming would be overwritten by the next sync.

docs.title: BF-134 · every Loop remote command leaves an APNs connection open
docs.text:
lib/server/loop.js sendNotification built new apn.Provider(options) near its start and called provider.send(...) at the end, without ever calling provider.shutdown(). In @parse/node-apn 5.2.3 a Provider's Client opens an HTTP/2 session to APNs on first send and keeps it open with a heartbeat ping every 60 s (config.heartBeat 60000, an unref'd setInterval in lib/client.js), until shutdown() clears both. On a server GOAWAY the library destroys the session but not the client, so the interval, which holds the client and its signed token, stays.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev 4d9ecc3b with tools/lab/apns-shutdown/probe.js, which points loop.js at a local HTTP/2 APNs stand-in (as the #8419 tests do) and counts sessions and live heartbeat intervals: after 1, 5 and 20 remote commands, 1, 5 and 20 of each remain; after the stand-in sends GOAWAY, 0 sessions remain but 20 intervals are still live. Controls: one push leaves 1 session; an explicit shutdown() leaves 0. A remote bolus that loop.js refuses after its checks still built a provider (1 interval). With no Loop settings at all, the call throws before building one. The same probe exits 0 on bf/loop-apns-shutdown. Not run: real APNs, and a long-running process's memory (session -6a's soak saw a higher resident size on the candidate, one sample, not attributed).

Found from #8419's new test hang: fakeAPNServer.close() waits for open sessions; Node 24 closes idle ones itself, 20 and 22 do not.

Fix (on bf/loop-apns-shutdown, 8046336d): build the provider just before the send and call provider.shutdown() in a finally on the send; refused commands no longer build one. tests/loop-apns-connections.test.js counts open sessions after three commands, after a refused push, and providers built for a refused bolus; all three fail on dev's loop.js. Full suite 3120/0/3 vs dev 3117/0/3 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43).

docs.title: BF-135 · a record AndroidAPS deletes keeps counting in COB, IOB and the chart
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8775 (merge 1157a8de, head 4658b233); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Found 2026-09-25 by the journey lab as JL-1 (journey lab §JL-1, journey map §B5).

Mechanism. AndroidAPS deletes by soft delete. Through API v3 it sends a DELETE, and the server sets isValid: false on the record; through its v1 client it sends a websocket dbUpdate that sets isValid: false. API v3 search and history honour the flag. Nothing else does: v1 reads still return the record, and the data loader, and with it COB, IOB and the chart, the server cache, /api/v1/profile/current and /api/v2/properties, keep counting it. Outside API v3, the only isValid check is for OpenAPS Offline (lib/data/ddata.js:351, the same on v15.0.8 and dev e3adc91d). Any API v3 client's DELETE is a soft delete, so the same holds for it.

Reproduced on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev e3adc91d in the journey lab, on a site with no device status so that COB comes from treatments: AndroidAPS-shaped carbs of 40 g (v3 POST) give COB 40; after the AndroidAPS v3 delete, COB is still 40. The same happens through the AndroidAPS v1 socket dbUpdate. Control (run on e3adc91d only): a v1 DELETE of the same record by _id leaves no COB. It exists on 15.0.8, so it is not a 15.0.9 regression. IOB was covered by the fix's tests; the chart glyph and the report totals were read, not run.

Severity. Safety, dosing-relevant display: Nightscout's COB and IOB, and what it hands to followers, are overstated by the deleted amount, with no error. Check COB and IOB in the app that doses. This is not medical advice.

Decision 2026-09-25 (maintainer): fixed in 15.0.9, with BF-122, on the same branch.

Fixed 2026-09-25 on local branch bf/v1-writes-v3-history 718efddc (the BF-122 commit; one commit on origin/dev e3adc91d, not pushed). lib/server/soft-deleted.js: a record with isValid: false counts as deleted everywhere except v3 search and history: v1 list, count and single-entry reads, profile/current, food lists, the data loader's loads (COB, IOB, the chart, the websocket data), the cache (an update to isValid: false evicts the record), and the websocket dbAdd dedup lookups. A read that names isValid in find gets what it asks for. A v1 DELETE still removes soft-deleted records. An entry re-sent for a deleted reading is stored again, as a treatment and a v3 POST are. COB goes from 40 to none on both delete paths (tests/soft-deleted.jl1.test.js, which also covers IOB, a deleted profile, glucose reading, device status and food, and the cache).

docs.title: BF-136 · API v3 refuses an AndroidAPS write that lands on a record written through v1
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8776 (merge 13f235e9, head 962d189b); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Mechanism. A v3 POST with no identifier looks for an existing record by the collection's fallback fields (treatments: created_at + eventType, lib/api3/generic/setup.js:95) and, when it finds one, becomes an update of that record (lib/api3/generic/create/operation.js:43, :52, isDeduplication: true). The update validator (lib/api3/generic/update/validate.js:21-43) lists identifier, date, utcOffset, eventType, device, app, srvCreated, subject, srvModified, modifiedBy and isValid as fields a client may not change, and exempts only identifier during deduplication. A record written through v1 has no app, device or isValid; a careportal-shaped one has no date either. An AndroidAPS record has them, so the comparison fails and the POST is answered 400.

Corrected 2026-09-26 (measured while fixing; the first version of this section said the refusal was always on app):

  • A careportal-shaped v1 record is refused on date, because careportal records have no date. The refusal is on app ("Field app cannot be modified by the client") only when the v1 record carries a date.
  • A v3 PUT of a v1-born record is refused on date, whether or not app is sent.
  • A v3 PATCH carrying isValid: true, which AndroidAPS sends on every update, is refused with "Field isValid". So every AndroidAPS edit of a v1-born record was silently dropped, for example a careportal temp target that AndroidAPS changes.
  • Deletes are not affected.

What AndroidAPS does with the 400 (AndroidAPS 7e1d537d49, read): NSClientV3Plugin.kt:1019 logs "◄ FAIL" and falls through, and DataSyncSelectorV3.kt:256 advances the upload cursor, so AndroidAPS treats the 400 as final and does not retry the record (a 404 is retried; a 400 is not). The entry stays on the phone and never reaches Nightscout.

Reproduced 2026-09-25 on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev e3adc91d: a v1 treatment (Meal Bolus, 20 g carbs) at time T, then a v3 Meal Bolus at T from app AAPS with no identifier. The v3 write was answered 400 and the stored record stayed the v1 one. The v3 PUT refusal was measured on both builds (also recorded under OID-V3-EDIT-MERGE).

Severity. Safety, dosing-relevant data loss in Nightscout: the AndroidAPS entry is missing from Nightscout's COB, IOB, chart, reports and what followers see, and nothing on the site says so. The phone's own dosing is unaffected, because AndroidAPS keeps its own record. It needs the same created_at and eventType as a record written through v1, for example the same meal entered in the careportal and on the phone for the same time. BF-122's fix, which sends careportal entries to AndroidAPS, makes it more likely that both exist.

Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): fixed in 15.0.9.

Fixed 2026-09-26 on local branch bf/api3-app-field-v1-records df6c04bc (worktree externals/work/crm-r2-fix-136; one commit on dev e3adc91d, not pushed; Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43):

  • Rule (isSameAsStored in lib/api3/generic/update/validate.js, used by the POST dedup, PUT and PATCH): a field the stored record lacks is accepted when it contradicts nothing. app and device take their first value; isValid: true is accepted and false stays refused; date is accepted only if it equals the stored created_at instant. identifier, utcOffset, eventType and the server fields stay strict.
  • Probe api3-app-field.js: exit 1 on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev e3adc91d (3 of 13 arms refused), exit 0 on df6c04bc (13 of 13); its 15 controls pass on all three.
  • Tests. 16 new tests (tests/api3.v1-record-immutable-fields.test.js), 9 of which fail on dev; suite 3186/0/3, and 3212/0/3 merged with BF-122's 718efddc.
  • Trade-off, pinned by a test. With the fix, the v3 fallback dedup (created_at + eventType, amounts not compared) replaces a v1 record at the same millisecond: careportal 20 g becomes the AndroidAPS 30 g, and the careportal notes and enteredBy are lost. Before the fix the AndroidAPS entry was lost instead. Rare, because careportal times are whole minutes. With BF-121's fix as well, a later identical v1 re-send of the taken-over record no longer matches it and is stored again. Accepted by the maintainer 2026-09-26 as a known issue of 15.0.9, not a defect to fix for it (BF-121's detail).

docs.title: BF-137 · several IFTTT Maker keys break the order of an alarm's calls and the retry
docs.text:
Mechanism. MAKER_KEY (and MAKER_ANNOUNCEMENT_KEY) may hold several keys separated by spaces (lib/plugins/maker.js:10-14). makeRequests (:82-97) sends three events per alarm, ns-event, ns-<level> and ns-<level>-<plugin>, as three steps of async.series, which expects each step to call back once. makeKeyRequests (:98-104) calls makeKeyRequest for every key with the same callback, so a step with N keys calls back N times. In async 0.9.2 (the version package.json pins with ^0.9.2), each extra callback starts the next step again and calls the final callback again.

The final callback is sendMakerEvent's (lib/server/pushnotify.js:124-144). A success extends the alarm's dedup key from 30 s to 15 minutes (:141); an error leaves the 30-second key, which is BF-125's retry. With several keys, one key's success extends the key even when another key's call failed, so the failed key is not retried for 15 minutes.

Reproduced in-process 2026-09-25 with two keys against a local stand-in for IFTTT: an alarm made 6 requests in interleaved order, and the final callback ran 4 times. The reproduction script was in a scratch directory and was not retained. The missed retry follows from the 15-minute key and is read, not run. lib/plugins/maker.js and pushnotify.js are identical on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev e3adc91d (git diff is empty); bf/maker-level-names does not touch maker.js.

Severity. Low: an alarm to one of several Maker keys can be missed for up to 15 minutes when that key's call fails, and the three events arrive out of order. Bounded to sites with more than one Maker key.

Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): after 15.0.9.

Fix shape (not measured): have makeKeyRequests call back once, after every key's request has answered (for example with async.each), and report an error if any key failed, so the retry covers the failed key. A tests/maker.test.js case with two keys and a failing stub.

docs.title: BF-138 · /pebble in the other units computes the Bolus Wizard Preview against the wrong settings
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8777 (merge d613c35f, head 4864d679); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Mechanism. /pebble adds the Bolus Wizard Preview fields bwp and bwpo from the bwp plugin run on its own sandbox (lib/server/pebble.js:95-99). prepareSandbox (:143-154) switches that sandbox to mmol/L when the request asks for it (:146-148), but the profile's sensitivity and targets stay in the site's units. On an mg/dL site asked for ?units=mmol, the plugin compares an mmol/L reading with mg/dL settings.

Reproduced in-process 2026-09-25 on v15.0.8 and dev, through the pebble middleware and handler as for BF-128: sensitivity 70, targets 90-126, 1 U given 30 minutes before. The site's own values are bwp −0.96 and bwpo 23; ?units=mmol gives bwp −2.17 and bwpo −61.8. On an mmol/L site asked for mg/dL, bwpo stays in mmol/L next to an mg/dL reading, unlabelled. bf/pebble-delta-units aa224c69 does not change either.

Corrected 2026-09-26 on a booted server. The usual wrong output on an mg/dL site asked for mmol is bwp −0.96, right by coincidence, with bwpo 23.2: an mg/dL number in an mmol response. That is because of BF-139. The −2.17 / −61.8 pair appears only in-process on fresh data, or between a data load and its evaluation. On an mmol/L site asked for mg/dL, bwpo stayed in mmol/L (1.3) next to an mg/dL reading.

Severity. Safety, dosing-relevant display on a watch face: the bolus wizard preview is wrong in size and sign, and nothing marks it. Bounded to clients that ask /pebble for the units the site does not use. This is not medical advice; a dosing decision belongs to the app that doses.

Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): fixed in 15.0.9, with BF-128 and BF-139 on bf/pebble-delta-units, one PR. The fix must not switch the sandbox units the other way: BF-128's detail shows that gives a wrong bwp too.

Fixed 2026-09-26 on local branch bf/pebble-delta-units b3db0f36 (on b58b937c, BF-139, and aa224c69, BF-128; not pushed; Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43). iob, cob and bwp are computed in a sandbox in the site's units; bwpo is converted to the requested units; bwp, an insulin amount, is not converted. Across 18 combinations of site units and request, only bwp and bwpo change, in the two mismatched combinations, plus BF-128's delta. One BF-128 test expectation changed by design: bwpo now moves with ?units=mgdl. Suite on b3db0f36 3216/0/3, 25 new tests (4 for BF-139, 21 for BF-138).

docs.title: BF-139 · a /pebble request can leave glucose values scaled in its units for other readers
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8777 (merge d613c35f, head 4864d679); not released, goes into 15.0.9.

Described by mechanism only: it is live on 15.0.8.

Mechanism (read). The sandbox a /pebble request builds works on the server's data through ddata.clone(), which is a shallow copy (lib/data/ddata.js:109-111): the reading objects are the server's own. sbx.scaleEntry (lib/sandbox.js:258-268), which bgnow calls for each reading (lib/plugins/bgnow.js:85), writes entry.scaled onto the reading when it is not already set. A request whose units differ from the site's (prepareSandbox, lib/server/pebble.js:143-154) can therefore leave the readings carrying a scaled value in its units, and until the next data load replaces those objects, other readers of the same objects can see values in the wrong units. The code is the same on v15.0.8 92d08342 and dev e3adc91d.

Reach (2026-09-26). It reaches the server's own alarm evaluation (reproduced on a booted server 2026-09-26). The evaluation after a data load reads a scaled value left by a /pebble request in other units, so it could judge a reading in the wrong units and raise a false low alarm; values shown by /api/v2/properties, Alexa and Google Home could be wrong until the next data load. Severity raised to safety (alarm integrity).

Disclosure decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): public PR, with the mechanism and outcome in the body and no reproduction recipe (no request pattern, timing, permission or trigger values), the BF-70 / #8743 precedent. Reproduction detail stays out of the public repo while 15.0.8 is the current release.

Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): fixed in 15.0.9, with BF-128 and BF-138 on bf/pebble-delta-units, one PR.

Fixed 2026-09-26 on local branch bf/pebble-delta-units b58b937c (on aa224c69; not pushed): the /pebble sandbox gets its own copies of the readings, without a stored scaled value, so a /pebble request no longer writes onto the server's readings.

docs.title: BF-140 · on dev after #8758, API v3 cannot delete a v1 record whose identifier is null or ""
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 via PR #8778 (AndyLow91, outside contributor; merge aa1111b2, head 18141136, fix 15f01f33); not released, goes into 15.0.9. Filed from the PR, credited to its author; the programme reproduced it independently and reviewed the fix.

Mechanism. API v1 stores a treatment with the identifier it is sent when that is a string or null (validateDedupFields in lib/server/treatments.js refuses any other type); v1 entries and devicestatus store any value. API v3 reads pass every record through normalizeDoc, which replaces a falsy identifier (absent, null, "", 0) with the _id, so a client listing or getting such a record addresses it by its _id. GET and the pre-delete check use filterForOne, which matches by _id whatever the identifier is. The delete itself (deleteEveryForm / updateEveryForm) uses filterForEveryForm, which #8758's cb7d4110 (for BF-117) restricted to records without an identifier field, so that a record with an identifier of its own is not reached through its _id. A stored null or "" is a field, so the delete matched nothing and answered 404.

Reproduced 2026-09-26 with api3-empty-identifier-delete.js (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43; a booted server, synthetic records, v1 POST then v3 by _id):

tree identifier absent (control) null "" exit v15.0.8 92d08342 GET 200, soft 200, permanent 200 same same 0 dev 750801a9 (before #8778) GET 200 (= _id), soft 200, permanent 200; v1 lists 1 → 0; COB 30 → 0 GET 200 (= _id), soft 404, permanent 404, record kept and valid; v1 lists 1 → 1; COB 30 → 30 same as null 1 dev aa1111b2 (#8778) and ff93fa94 as before soft 200, permanent 200; v1 lists 1 → 0; COB 30 → 0 same 0

The same holds for an entry stored with null or "" (soft DELETE 404 on 750801a9, 200 on the others). On v15.0.8 a soft delete does not hide the record from v1 or COB at all (BF-135); after

docs.title: 8775 it does, which is what makes a refused delete matter: an AndroidAPS delete of such a record
docs.text:
(AndroidAPS NSClientV3 deletes by v3 soft DELETE, addressing a v1 record by the _id v3 returned) would be logged as failed and the carbs or insulin would keep counting on the site. #8778's own test file fails 14 of 31 tests on 750801a9 and passes on aa1111b2.

Reach (read, 2026-09-26). No client in externals/ writes identifier: null or "" in normal operation. AndroidAPS serialises with explicitNulls = false, so a null identifier is omitted (core/nssdk/.../NsSdkJson.kt); it would echo "" only if the server returned "", which normalizeDoc never does. Nocturne's v1 write-back sends identifier as an alias of its id and could send null or "" only for a record without one. nightscout-connect sends a non-empty identifier; Loop/NightscoutKit, Trio, xDrip+, xdripswift, nightguard and the others omit it. AndroidAPS is the only corpus client that deletes through API v3 (soft, without ?permanent).

Review of the fix. The fallback now matches identifier: {$in: [null, ""], $not: {$type: "array"}} beside _id equal to a form of the requested identifier. $in: [null] also matches an absent field, so the old case is kept. Every fallback clause still pins _id to the requested value, so no unrelated record can match; the array exclusion only decides whether the record whose _id was asked for is reached, and #8778 pins that an array identifier (for example ["", "other"]) keeps its record out of the _id fallback. The guard that motivated cb7d4110 holds: a record with its own identifier is still not deleted through its _id (404, soft and permanent, on aa1111b2 and ff93fa94; v15.0.8 deleted it). It is consistent with #8775's lib/server/soft-deleted.js (the refused delete was the only reason such a record kept counting) and does not touch #8776's validate.js rule, which keeps identifier immutable on update.

Left, measured on ff93fa94; filed 2026-09-26 as BF-142 and BF-141. (1) A record whose stored identifier is 0 or an array ([null], [""], ["", "other"]), which v1 entries and devicestatus accept, is still returned by v3 GET under its _id and refused by v3 DELETE with 404: normalizeDoc treats 0 as empty and the fallback does not, and an array is excluded by design. No client is known to write these. (2) With

docs.title: 8780 (BF-121), a v1 treatment re-sent with identifier: "" is stored twice (the same POST twice:
docs.text: 2 records on ff93fa94, 1 on v15.0.8, 750801a9 and aa1111b2): treatment-fallback-key.js keys a write without identity on identifier: null, which matches an absent or null field but not "", while upsertQueryFor treats "" as no identifier. null and absent re-sends are unchanged. Whether "" should count as no identity everywhere, as #8778 now does for deletes, is for the maintainer. Decided 2026-09-26: (2) is BF-141, fixed for 15.0.9; (1) is BF-142, after 15.0.9 (reversed the same day: BF-142 is fixed for 15.0.9).

docs.title: BF-141 · on dev after #8780, a treatment re-sent with an empty identity is stored twice — merged 2026-09-26 (PR #8781)
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 through PR #8781 (AndyLow91, merge ce7d754a, fix a28fcecb); not released, goes into 15.0.9. Found in the review of #8778 (BF-140). Never released: present on dev from #8780's merge ff93fa94 to ce7d754a. Our fix, bf/fallback-key-empty-identifier aaf67785 (PR #8782), was closed as superseded on 2026-09-26.

#8781's rule. The no-identity clause matches each of the five fields with {$in: [null, ""], $not: {$type: 'array'}}: the same forms as ours, and it also refuses a stored array such as ["", "abc"], which $in would otherwise match through its "" element although the record has a real identity. #8775's in-memory pre-read (srv-dates matches) learned the same selector in that PR (see BF-143). Measured 2026-09-26 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43): #8782's tests/api.same-time-treatments.test.js (89 tests, the 71 for BF-141 among them) passes 89/0 on ce7d754a without #8782's change.

The rest of this section is the record of our fix as it stood before #8781.

Mechanism. BF-121 made the API v1 and websocket fallback key (created_at + eventType) identity-aware in lib/server/treatment-fallback-key.js. A write that carries none of syncIdentifier, id, uuid, NSCLIENT_ID — where present() counts absent, null and "" alike as none — matches only a record without identity, and upsertQueryFor sends a write whose identifier is "" to that fallback (if (obj.identifier)). But the stored side of the rule was {field: {$eq: null}} for those four fields and identifier, which matches null or absent and not "". v1 stores identifier: "" as sent, so the second POST of the same record did not match the first and was inserted. The same holds for a record stored with any of the four client fields as "". The websocket dbAdd exact match builds its query with the same helper; its similar match (same amounts within 2 s) hid the gap for an identical re-send, but not for a re-send with another amount, which the no-identity exact match answers with the stored record.

Fix. The no-identity clause now matches each of the five fields with {$in: [null, ""]} (a fresh object per query; the list is the server's own, not client input). A write without identity therefore matches a stored record whose field is absent, null or "", as a null write already matched null or absent. A write with a non-empty identity is unchanged: that value must be equal, so a real identity and "" are still two records. API v3 is not changed.

Measured 2026-09-26 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43 in a dedicated container):

  • tests/api.same-time-treatments.test.js, new describe "an empty identity is no identity (BF-141)", 71 tests: every stored form (absent, null, "") by every re-sent form for the five fields through v1; a record inserted with "" before the change; the socket exact match for four fields by three stored forms; controls (a real identity kept apart from "" both ways, an API v3 record not replaced, different carbs with "" kept as two, a socket write with a real id not answered by a record with id: ""). 29 fail on ff93fa94 (2 records where 1 was expected; 3 where 2), all pass on aaf67785. Reverting only the query line turns the same 29 red.
  • Two literal-selector expectations change, marked in the tests (tests/storage.selector-hardening.test.js, tests/websocket.input-validation.test.js).
  • Full suite on aaf67785, fresh database: 3467 passing / 0 failing / 3 pending (ff93fa94: 3396/0/3; +71).
  • same-time-resend-shapes.js ff93fa94 against aaf67785: every row the same (I8185, D01, D04 and D05 kept 2; R01 to R21 unchanged; R18, D02 and D03 as before); exit 0. same-time-carbs.js: the same output on both, exit 0.
  • api3-empty-identifier-delete.js: the only difference between ff93fa94 and aaf67785 is the "" re-send line (stored 2 → 1); v15.0.8 92d08342 stores 1 for every shape.

Reach (read). No client in the corpus is known to send an empty identifier or client id; null and absent re-sends were not affected.

docs.title: BF-142 · on dev since #8758, API v3 cannot delete a record whose identifier is 0 or an array
docs.text:
Fixed 2026-09-26 on local branch bf/api3-delete-nonstring-identifier 1c3aeb8c, one commit on official/dev ce7d754a (not pushed), for 15.0.9. Filed the same day as deferred past 15.0.9; the maintainer reversed that on 2026-09-26. Found in the review of #8778 (BF-140); point (1) of that section's "Left" paragraph.

Mechanism. API v1 entries and devicestatus store any identifier value they are sent, including 0 and arrays; v1 treatments refuse a non-string one. API v3 reads pass every record through normalizeDoc, which shows a falsy identifier (0 included) as the _id; GET and the pre-delete check use filterForOne, which matches the _id whatever the stored identifier is. The delete itself uses filterForEveryForm, which reaches a record through its _id only where identifier is absent (#8758's cb7d4110, for BF-117, so that a record with an identifier of its own is not deleted through its _id), and since #8778 also null or "", excluding arrays by design. A stored 0 or array is neither, so soft and permanent DELETE match nothing and answer 404; the record stays valid.

15.0.8. Its v3 delete used filterForOne for the existence check and the delete, so any record addressed by its hex _id was reached whatever its identifier (the same rule that let it delete a record with an identifier of its own, which BF-117 removed). Read at 92d08342 (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js filterForOne, modify.js deleteOne/updateOne) and run.

Reproduced 2026-09-26 with api3-empty-identifier-delete.js (its printed-only arms; Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43):

tree treatments inserted directly: [null], ["","other"], 0 v1 entries and devicestatus: 0, [null], [""] v15.0.8 92d08342 GET 200, soft DELETE 200, isValid false GET 200, soft DELETE 200, isValid false dev ff93fa94 (and aaf67785) GET 200, soft DELETE 404, record kept GET 200, soft DELETE 404, record kept

Reach (read). No client in the corpus is known to write these identifier shapes; AndroidAPS, the only corpus client that deletes through v3, sends string identifiers and omits a null one.

Fix (1c3aeb8c). filterForEveryForm's _id fallback takes exactly the stored identifiers normalizeDoc (!doc.identifier) replaces by the _id: absent or null, "", 0 (any numeric zero, -0 included), false and NaN ({$in: [null, "", 0, false, NaN]}). The values normalizeDoc keeps are the record's own identifier, which v3 GET shows, and stay out of the fallback as before: a non-empty string (BF-117), arrays (#8778; $in would otherwise match their elements) and Decimal128 (the driver returns it as an object, which is truthy). Every fallback clause still requires the _id to be a form of the requested id. Storage, reads, PUT and PATCH are unchanged. The rule, stated as the tests pin it: when v3 GET shows the _id as a record's identifier, soft and permanent DELETE by that _id find it; when GET shows a stored identifier, DELETE by the _id does not.

Tests (tests/api3.delete-every-form.test.js, 30 new, real MongoDB 7.0.43, Node 22.23.2). Soft and permanent DELETE of treatments (seeded directly with 0, -0, false, NaN), entries and devicestatus (written through API v1 with 0 and false; JSON cannot carry -0 or NaN) after GET shows the _id as the identifier: 16, all red on ce7d754a with GET 200 then DELETE 404. Records whose own identifier is [null], [""], ["","other"], [0], Decimal128 0 or a string are refused through their _id, soft and permanent: 12, green on both. A DELETE of one record leaves records with identifier null, "", 0, false, NaN, [null], [""], ["","other"], [0] or none under other _ids untouched: 2 (red on ce7d754a only because the target, stored with 0, is refused). Break-its, one at a time: without 0 in the list 10 red, without false 6, without NaN 2, without the array exclusion 12 (#8778's four array tests and eight new ones), without the Decimal128 exclusion 2, without the _id clause 4 (the two bystander tests and two BF-117 twin tests). Full suite 3458/0/3 on a fresh database (ce7d754a 3428/0/3).

Probe on three trees (same probe, Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43):

stored identifier v15.0.8 92d08342 dev ce7d754a fix 1c3aeb8c 0, false (treatments direct; entries and devicestatus through v1) GET shows _id; soft and permanent DELETE 200 GET shows _id; DELETE 404 GET shows _id; DELETE 200 [null], [""], ["","other"] (same collections) GET shows the array; DELETE 200 GET shows the array; DELETE 404 GET shows the array; DELETE 404 absent, null, ""; a record with its own string identifier DELETE 200; the string-identifier record is deleted through its _id DELETE 200; the string-identifier record 404 (BF-117) the same as ce7d754a bystanders under other _ids - untouched untouched

The fix differs from v15.0.8 only for arrays and the string identifier, the records whose identifier v3 GET shows as stored. No v3 read shows such a record's _id, so a v3 client cannot learn the id it would delete by. If the maintainer wants arrays deletable by _id as on 15.0.8, that is a change to the exclusion, and it would also delete the record in #8778's array test.

Left, not changed here (read and run on all three trees). API v3 PATCH and PUT by the _id of a record stored with identifier null, "" or 0 do not find it: they use identifyingFilter, whose _id fallback needs the identifier absent (read, so any falsy identifier; run for null, "" and 0). PATCH answers 404 and PUT inserts a second record (201, two stored), while GET shows that _id as the identifier. The same on v15.0.8 92d08342, ce7d754a and 1c3aeb8c, so not a regression; filed as BF-145 (after 15.0.9).

docs.title: BF-143 · on dev after #8780, an identical treatment re-send rewrites srvCreated — merged 2026-09-26 (PR #8781)
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 through PR #8781 by AndyLow91, an outside contributor (merge ce7d754a, fix a28fcecb); not released, goes into 15.0.9. Present on dev from #8780's merge ff93fa94 to ce7d754a; never released.

Mechanism. Since #8775 (BF-122), a v1 treatment write keeps the stored record's srvCreated by reading the stored documents its replaceOne filters name before the write (srv-dates carryForReplace), one query per 500 items, and deciding in memory which stored document each filter names (matches, sameValue). sameValue(stored, want) returned false whenever either side was null or absent. #8780 (BF-121) gave a write without identity a filter that includes {$eq: null} for syncIdentifier, id, uuid, NSCLIENT_ID and identifier (and for carbs or insulin when the write has none). MongoDB's {$eq: null} matches an absent field; the in-memory match did not, and it answered "no match" rather than "ask MongoDB", so no stored record was found. carry then stamped srvCreated as for a new record, and replaceOne, which MongoDB evaluates, matched the stored record and replaced it with the new srvCreated. The stored _id is kept, since replaceOne does not change it.

Not affected. A write that carries an identity (its filter names only present values), a v1 PUT (its filter is the _id), and the socket dbAdd (it updates with $set, not a replacement). Measured below.

Fix (#8781). sameValue treats a wanted null as equal to an absent field, as MongoDB does; matches evaluates the new empty-identity selector (BF-141) in memory, and hands any array comparison back to MongoDB.

Reproduced 2026-09-26 with retry-keeps-srvcreated.js (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43 in a dedicated container; synthetic 20 g treatments; each arm writes once, reads the stored document, waits 20 ms and re-sends):

arm v15.0.8 92d08342 aa1111b2 (#8775, not #8780) ff93fa94 (before #8781) ce7d754a (after) R1 v1 POST, no identity; identical re-POST 1 record, _id kept, no srvCreated kept srvCreated +41 ms, _id kept kept R2 the same, re-POST as [it] no srvCreated kept +31 ms kept R3 the same, re-POST as [it, a new one] no srvCreated kept +30 ms kept R4 carbs + insulin, no identity; re-POST no srvCreated kept +37 ms kept R5 with uuid; re-POST (control) no srvCreated kept kept kept R6 with identifier; re-POST (control) no srvCreated kept kept kept R7 v1 PUT of the document v1 GET returns no srvCreated kept kept kept R8 v1 PUT without srvCreated/srvModified no srvCreated kept kept kept R9 socket dbAdd identical re-send no srvCreated kept kept kept

Every arm on every tree stores one record and keeps its _id; srvModified moves on every v1 re-send and not on the socket re-send, on all three dev trees. Probe exit 1 (a FAIL row on ff93fa94 only).

Against #8781's description. It says retries "retain the original _id and srvCreated". In these arms the _id was never lost on ff93fa94; only srvCreated moved. A lost _id (a second record) is the empty-identity case, BF-141. It dates the regression to "after #8775 and #8780": it needs both, and aa1111b2 (after #8775, before #8780) does not show it.

Reach (read). AndroidAPS maps srvCreated into its model; no use of it in a decision was found. The creation time is informational; history and sync use srvModified.

docs.title: BF-144 · on dev after #8775, a restart after a large import can hide new records from API v3 history — merged 2026-09-26 (PR #8781)
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 through PR #8781 by AndyLow91, an outside contributor (merge ce7d754a, fix a28fcecb); not released, goes into 15.0.9. Present on dev from #8775's merge 1157a8de to ce7d754a; never released.

Mechanism. #8775 (BF-122) gave every server write a srvModified from one process-wide clock, srv-dates next(), which never returns a value twice and never goes back: two writes in the same millisecond get consecutive values, so a v1 batch of N documents ends about N ms ahead of wall time, and later writes continue from there. API v3 history returns records with srvModified > cursor, and a reader (AndroidAPS NSClientV3) takes the largest value it received as its next cursor. Within one process that is safe. But the clock was only a variable: after a restart it began again from wall time, which could still be behind the cursor a reader had taken from the batch. A record written then got a srvModified below that cursor, and history never returned it.

Fix (#8781). At boot, before authorization, uploaders and the API start, the clock is set from the largest numeric srvModified stored in the six v3 collections (entries, treatments, devicestatus, profile, food, settings; configured collection names honoured; one indexed read per collection). A failure of that read is a boot error. Later writes continue above it.

Reproduced 2026-09-26 with history-clock-restart.js (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43 in a dedicated container; synthetic sgv entries): 30,000 entries through v1 in three back-to-back requests of 10,000 (the v1 maximum), v3 entries history read to the end by ETag (limit=1000), SIGTERM, restart on the same database, one entry through v3 and one through v1, history read from the saved cursor.

tree clock lead after the batch history read writes after restart, relative to the cursor history from the cursor v15.0.8 92d08342 none: v1 entries get no srvModified 0 records (v1 records are not in history, BF-122) v3 write at wall time v3 record only; not the defect's precondition aa1111b2 (#8775) 26,423 ms 30 pages, 30,000 records v3 −24,763 ms, v1 −24,755 ms 0 records ff93fa94 (before #8781) 25,201 ms 30 pages, 30,000 records v3 −23,553 ms, v1 −23,547 ms 0 records ce7d754a (after) 25,592 ms 30 pages, 30,000 records v3 +1 ms, v1 +2 ms both records

Restarts took 0.8-1.0 s. The writes happened 23.6-24.8 s before wall time reached the cursor, so the window after such a restart is as long as the clock lead; a batch of 60,000 gave a lead of 53 s. Probe exit 1 (FAIL rows on aa1111b2 and ff93fa94).

Against #8781's description. None found. Its reproduction (30,000 readings, all history pages, restart, a v3 write; history empty before, returning it after) is what the probe shows, and the v1 write behaves the same.

Left (read). A reader whose cursor is ahead of every stored srvModified (a hard-deleted record's, or a clock rollback with a cursor from another server) is outside the restored value;

docs.title: 8781 says it does not change the hard-delete and pre-commit history semantics.
BF-145 · API v3 PATCH and PUT by the shown id miss a record whose identifier is null, "" or 0
docs.text:
Mechanism. API v3 shows a record's _id as its identifier when the stored identifier is falsy (normalizeDoc, !doc.identifier). DELETE now finds such a record by that id (filterForEveryForm, BF-140 and BF-142). PATCH and PUT use a different helper, identifyingFilter (lib/api3/storage/mongoCollection/utils.js, used by modify.js), whose _id fallback applies only when the identifier field is absent. For a record stored with null, "" or 0, PATCH by the shown id matches nothing and answers 404; PUT matches nothing and inserts a new record, so two are stored.

Measured 2026-09-26 by the BF-142 fix work on v15.0.8 92d08342, dev ce7d754a and 1c3aeb8c (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43): identical on all three, for null, "" and 0. Not a regression from 15.0.8.

Reach. No client in the corpus is known to write these identifiers in normal use; AndroidAPS omits a null identifier and edits through PATCH by the identifier v3 gave it.

Fix shape (not built). Give identifyingFilter the same falsy-identifier rule as filterForEveryForm, keeping BF-117's guard (a record with its own non-empty identifier is not reachable through its _id) and the requirement that _id equals a form of the requested id. Decide separately whether a PUT to such an id should replace the record.

Decision 2026-09-26 (maintainer): file for after 15.0.9.

docs.title: BF-146 · API v3 treatments are held in memory without mills — merged 2026-09-26 (PR #8784)
docs.text:
Merged 2026-09-26 through PR #8784 (merge ce30a94d, head d235bdf6; commits db99bba4 treatments and d235bdf6 device status); not released, goes into 15.0.9. RC run 020 on ce30a94d: 3473/0/3 in six cells (Node 20, 22, 24 × MongoDB 4.4, 7.0), the 15 new titles the only difference from 699eb5fa; tools/lab/rc-soak/probe-v3-late-mills.js exits 0 on ce30a94d and 1 on 699eb5fa and v15.0.8, where a late v3 bolus leaves IOB at 0, late v3 carbs leave COB at 0 and a late v3 device status is missing from the default v1 read, all three present after a restart.

Mechanism. Every v1 write path in lib/server/treatments.js emits its documents to the server's cache through ddata.processRawDataForRuntime, which adds mills (from created_at) and endmills (from a duration). The API v3 storage wrapper (lib/api3/storage/mongoCachedCollection/index.js, updateInCache) emitted the stored document as it is. The cache keeps such a record (its age falls back to date). The dataloader builds the treatments from the cache and, once the cache holds enough treatments, refetches from MongoDB only its most recent minutes; a record inside that window comes back with mills and replaces the cached copy, a record dated before it does not. So a late v3 upload, or a v3 edit (PUT or PATCH) of an older record, is held without mills until restart or until it leaves the cache's retention.

  • lib/plugins/iob.js counts a treatment only when mills <= time and cob.js only when mills < time: the record counts in neither.
  • The dataloader sorts the treatments with a.mills - b.mills; with one record lacking mills the comparator returns NaN and the array is not in time order. cob.js takes "last carbs" in array order (BF-133) and chains each carb entry's decay on the one before it in array order, so an already absorbed entry processed after a newer one is counted again.
  • The page data the websocket sends to the browser is the same array, so the browser's own IOB and COB (the same plugins) are affected in the same way.

Measured 2026-09-26 (Node 22.23.2, MongoDB 7.0.43, fresh test databases), with the branch's test file on three trees: v15.0.8 92d08342, dev 699eb5fa and bf/api3-cache-derived-fields db99bba4. On both unfixed trees, with enough treatments held for the incremental load: a late v3 bolus gives treatment IOB 0 and late v3 carbs COB 0 (the same on the page data sent over the socket, and after a v3 PATCH and PUT of an older bolus); with mixed v1 and v3 writes the loaded treatments come out in reverse time order; with an older (absorbed) and a newer carb entry and one late v3 record, "last carbs" names the older entry and COB is 34.5 g where the same records in time order give 10 g. A v1 bolus of the same age and a v3 bolus dated now are counted on every tree. On db99bba4 all nine tests pass.

Other v3-cached collections (checked). The cache holds treatments, entries and device status. Entries: the dataloader builds each reading's mills from date, and v1's in-memory entries read sets mills from date; measured with a late v3 reading and more held readings than the default read, the reading is in its place in GET /api/v1/entries and in the page's glucose data, so entries are passed on as before. Device status: the dataloader adds mills to its own copy, so the pills and the page data are not affected; but GET /api/v1/devicestatus served from memory (no query other than count) sorts the cached records by mills (missing counts as 0), so a late v3 device status is placed after every record that has one. Measured on 699eb5fa and v15.0.8: with 24 held v1 statuses, a v3 status newer than all of them was missing from the default read; with the whole held set requested it came back last instead of first.

Fix. The v3 wrapper passes treatments and device status through ddata.processRawDataForRuntime before emitting them, so they enter the cache exactly as a v1 write's do. Nothing stored changes: the helper derives on a copy (the v1 paths store no mills either). In GET /api/v1/treatments served from memory, a v3 record now carries mills (and endmills or a derived duration where the v1 helper adds them), as v1-written records there already do; its order is unchanged, since the cache already ordered it by date. In GET /api/v1/devicestatus served from memory, a v3 status carries mills and takes its place by time; the set of records for a given count is otherwise the same, and a late v3 status can now be inside the count where it was left out. Device status was added on 2026-09-26 (maintainer decision, for consistency with the v1 paths).

Tests. tests/api3.cache-derived-fields.test.js, 15 tests on a real MongoDB. Red on 699eb5fa and v15.0.8 (10): a late v3 bolus in IOB, late v3 carbs in COB, a late v3 bolus after PATCH and PUT, the page data over the socket, time order with mixed v1 and v3 writes, "last carbs" after an edit (BF-133), the COB total against the time-ordered one; a late v3 status in the default v1 device status read, the whole held set read in time order, and the same with DENORMALIZE_DATES on (which rewrites created_at in place on the cached records; mills still matches the record's time over repeated reads). Green on all trees (5): a v1 bolus of the same age, a v3 bolus dated now, a v1 status of the same age in its place, a v3 status dated now first, and the page data holding the late v3 status with its time. Break-it: deriving the fields and then dropping mills gives the same red (7 for treatments, 3 for device status); deriving them only on create turns the PATCH/PUT test red; leaving device status out (db99bba4) gives the 3 device status tests red. Full suite 3473/0/3 on a fresh database (699eb5fa 3458/0/3; db99bba4 3467/0/3), no existing test changed. Treatment probes (same-time-carbs, same-time-resend-shapes, retry-keeps-srvcreated, v1-writes-v3-history) give the same output on 699eb5fa, db99bba4 and d235bdf6; v1-writes-v3-history exits 1 on its v1 DELETE arm on all of them.

Not measured. Chart placement (the renderer uses a record's own date before mills), temporary basals from v3 in the basal display, and reports (which read MongoDB, not the cache). Older releases: the v3 wrapper emits the stored document since 14.1.0 (read, not run).

docs.title: BF-147 · two overrides hold ajv and request's form-data inside advisory ranges
docs.text:
overrides["ajv@^6.0.0"] = "6.12.6" was set by 907fc5b4 ("Fix dev-mode bundle after PR #8518 merge: scope ajv overrides by version", 2026-05-14). GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 (ReDoS with the $data option) was published on 2026-02-11 and ajv 6.14.0, its fix for the 6.x line, on 2026-02-20, so the value was inside the advisory's range when it was written. overrides.request["form-data"] = "2.5.5" came with 5ab0af7a (2026-05-10), when 2.5.5 was the newest 2.x; form-data 2.5.6 was released on 2026-06-12 and GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx (CRLF injection through multipart field names and filenames) was published on 2026-06-15, so this pin went stale after it was written. Both are on v15.0.8 and on dev 295f1177.

Because overrides takes precedence over every declared range, npm audit cannot propose the patch releases: it reports form-data (and through it request, minimed-connect-to-nightscout and share2nightscout-bridge) as having no fix, and the ajv finding (with har-validator, schema-utils, style-loader, eslint and @eslint/eslintrc) as needing style-loader 4, a major. Nothing reports that the override is the cause. This is the BF-43 and BF-87 mechanism a third time.

Reach. ajv 6 is loaded by webpack loader option validation (schema-utils), by eslint, and by har-validator inside request. The webpack schemas are the repository's own configuration. form-data 2.x is reached only through request, which only minimed-connect-to-nightscout (mmconnect) and share2nightscout-bridge load; in 15.0.9 the bridge runs only with DEXCOM_BRIDGE_USE_LEGACY=true (lib/server/bootevent.js, lib/server/bridge-connect-compat.js). Neither package builds a multipart body (read from node_modules/share2nightscout-bridge/index.js and node_modules/minimed-connect-to-nightscout/nightscout.js). Exploitability through Nightscout is not measured; severity low.

Merged 2026-09-27 via PR #8786 (merge 7000eb18, 20:40Z; head 64a9cc13 on bf/override-advisory-pins, one commit on 295f1177). npm audit --package-lock-only on origin/dev 7000eb18: 7 (7 moderate), 5 with --omit=dev. The fix as run before the push: override values 6.14.0 and 2.5.6, then npm update browserslist baseline-browser-mapping postcss-selector-parser (their fixes are inside the declared ranges; the lockfile is stale, no override is involved). npm audit --package-lock-only goes from 17 (1 low, 13 moderate, 3 high) to 7 (7 moderate). Nine lockfile versions change, all patch or minor: ajv 6.12.6 → 6.14.0, request/node_modules/form-data 2.5.5 → 2.5.6, browserslist 4.28.2 → 4.29.1, baseline-browser-mapping 2.10.29 → 2.11.26, postcss-selector-parser 7.1.1 → 7.1.6, and caniuse-lite, electron-to-chromium, node-releases, update-browserslist-db with them. npm ci and the bundle build succeed (webpack 5.106.2, 3 warnings, as in RC runs 018 to 020); the full suite is 3473 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending on Node 24.15.0 with MongoDB 7.0.43 (a dedicated container, version read with db.version()), the same as RC run 020. Only one Node/MongoDB cell was run. The commit adds tests/dependency-overrides.test.js, which checks the resolved ajv 6 copies (under har-validator, style-loader's schema-utils and eslint) and request's form-data, and that form-data escapes line breaks in multipart field names and filenames: 5/5 on the branch, 0/5 on 295f1177's installed tree, each failing on the old version or the unescaped header. It was written after the suite run and was run on its own.

On the modernization line the question disappears: rh/cut2 02205d91 has neither finding, and rh/cut4 135faa3b, rh/cut35 cd93d8e8 and cut 5 b1bdaca0 audit at 0 including dev dependencies.

A gate that fails when an overrides value satisfies a published advisory range would have caught BF-87 and this entry; tools/qc/connector-pin-agreement-gate.js (which found BF-43) checks declared ranges only.

docs.title: 3. How to use this register
docs.text:
1. Anything found while doing multitenancy work that is also broken today gets an entry here, at the time it is found, with its evidence link. The register is the mechanism that keeps that promise.
  2. Prefer landing these independently. Each one is small, each ships to every current operator, and none needs a tenancy decision.
  3. Release-note the behaviour changes. BF-02 and BF-03 change what queries return. That is the point, and it should arrive as a documented fix. The note is in cgm-remote-monitor's CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] / Fixed, naming the collections and fields whose results change, with before/after examples.
  4. Keep severities honest. "Wrong answer with HTTP 200" is worse than "slow", and both are worse than "noisy". The table is sorted by that, not by effort.
  5. Allocate an id by reading the highest in §1/§1b at the moment you write it — never the one your brief quoted, because concurrent sessions file here.
  6. Check it is not a restatement before you file it. BF-12 is closed as invalid and is kept rather than deleted precisely because a deleted wrong entry gets raised again. Several of the entries filed on 2026-09-15 began as separate proposals and were merged into one, or folded into an existing entry as an amendment — the bulkUpsert scope findings amend BF-21 rather than taking ids, and three separate "everything says 15.0.9" proposals became one BF-60.
  7. Put it in §1 or §1b by the ships-to-operators-today test, not by how important it feels. §1 means present in what an operator runs today, which is master / 15.0.8 — not dev, not a cut branch, not an unmerged bf/* branch. That test is the only thing making §1 mean anything, and widening it would cost more than the entries it would admit.
  8. Say whether a prescribed fix has been run. An unrun prescription is marked UNVERIFIED in place rather than left to look settled.

docs.title: 4. Where this file sits
docs.text:
document relationship execution plan the reasoning, the decisions and the task definitions. Its §0 is the map of every other document queue/work-queue.yaml, queue/QUEUE.md, queue/README.md authoritative for item STATE, because its state is measured by a gate rather than asserted by an editor. This register is authoritative for defect facts and ids PR sequencing how the ten Phase 0 branches land maintainer release brief the same batch, presented as one decision semver and release versioning policy what version number each of these fixes forces

One gap in that policy is worth knowing while reading this file. Its surface ladder has no question for what the client computes and shows a person, so BF-35 — the bolus calculator's quick-pick chooser resolving the wrong record, graded high here — classifies as a patch under it and carries no operator-facing note obligation at all. The HTTP bytes are identical and the defect is entirely in the browser. BF-36 is the same case. The policy document records this as an open decision rather than silently adopting a fix; it is flagged here so that a severity in this register is not quietly downgraded by a version number somewhere else.

docs.title: BF-87 · the qs override holds the connector below its range and pins the server's query parser
docs.text:
overrides.qs = "6.15.1" and overrides.request.qs = "6.15.1" were added by 5ab0af7a ("Remediate runtime dependency CVEs", 2026-05-10), when 6.15.1 was the remedy. Since then the connector raised its own floor to ^6.15.3 and three advisories were published whose ranges include 6.15.1. overrides suppresses the ERESOLVE that would report the connector's range, so nothing says so — the BF-43 mechanism with a different package. Because the override is at the root, the single resolved copy is also the one express's and body-parser's query-string parsing uses, so the question is wider than the connector.

Not reproduced as a runtime failure or an exploit. What is asserted is the silent range violation and the advisory ranges.

Merged 2026-09-23 via PR #8749 (merge 9fd4600e; bf/qs-6.16 46b20b38): both override values are 6.16.0, the only version outside all three ranges. The documented query shapes parse identically and the suite is unchanged; only malformed bracket keys change. It changes the parser every request passes through.

docs.title: BF-88 · the modernization branch's TRUST_PROXY-unset default changes the client address in four cases
docs.text:
395f3207 ("Restore proxy compatibility by default", lib/server/client-ip.js on origin/chore/nightscout-modernization b1bdaca0) does not reproduce the address forwarded-for gives on origin/dev 74fc6619 in four cases: an IPv6 entry after the first in a comma-and-space X-Forwarded-For chain; an IPv4 address with a non-numeric port suffix; a request with no socket remote address; and a request carrying more than one forwarding-header family (dev's precedence depends on which family earlier requests used; the branch's order is fixed).

Reproduced by a differential probe. bf2/auth-hardening 8b975b41 pins dev's behaviour for the unset default, and restoring 395f3207's client-ip.js there fails exactly 7 of 48 tests/client-ip.test.js cases (re-run 2026-09-22). Severity: low — edge-case inputs, but the address is the failed-authentication delay's key and the setting is presented as compatibility-preserving, so an upgrader has no warning.

Decided 2026-09-23 (maintainer): the cuts keep 15.0.9's unset default, forwarded-for as on dev; 395f3207's fixed-precedence normalisation is not taken, and cut 5's four tests/client-ip.test.js expectations are replaced by 15.0.9's when the cuts are rebased. No flag for the other normalisation: with TRUST_PROXY unset the forwarding headers come from any peer, so neither answer is a security boundary; an address list (proxy-addr) is the deterministic path. The unset path is revisited when TRUST_PROXY's default is flipped.

docs.title: Phase 0: how to land ten branches as pull requests
docs.text:
Record

Record as of 2026-09-15. A point-in-time document; it is not kept up to date.

Snapshot, 2026-09-15/16, against cgm-remote-monitor origin/dev a8888f0d. Historical: the plan was carried out. Merged into dev: bf/merge #8734, bf/food #8735, bf/parms #8736, bf/coercion #8737, bf/reads #8738, bf/alarms #8739, bf/cache #8740. bf/auth (P0-C) and the BF-30 throttle (P0-J) are carried by #8754 bf2/auth-hardening, open. bf/connect-pin was replaced by #8762, which pins nightscout-connect exactly 0.1.0. Connector fix/connect-timer-jitter merged as nightscout-connect #68 and is in 0.1.0; no 0.0.14 exists. Nothing past 15.0.8 is released. Current state: queue/work-queue.yaml items P0-*, BF2-AUTH and RT-0, and the backfix register. Branch SHAs, pins and counts below are as of 2026-09-15/16.

Contributor-facing.

The plan is nine independent PRs onto dev, plus one independent PR in nightscout-connect (the earlier two-deep stack existed only because of a CHANGELOG.md collision, removed at the maintainer's instruction — §0b, §3a).

docs.title: The set, measured
docs.text:
Ten branches: nine in cgm-remote-monitor, one in nightscout-connect. All nine cgm-remote-monitor branches sit directly on origin/dev at a8888f0d in worktrees under externals/work/. There is no branch in this set based on another branch in this set.

repo branch tip commits what it is cgm-remote-monitor bf/alarms 5dcf783f 3 BF-28, BF-29, BF-31 — alarm delivery cgm-remote-monitor bf/auth 56ed29d2 3 BF-17, BF-30 — security. Third commit added 2026-09-16, see below cgm-remote-monitor bf/cache 4f86bab1 2 T0.2, T0.3 — cache clone cost cgm-remote-monitor bf/coercion b7234753 2 T0.5 — query filter typing, plus BF-40's $exists inversion. Amended and combined 2026-09-16, see below cgm-remote-monitor bf/connect-pin 0807eb1c 1 connector pin → the v0.0.14 tarball (one file, +1/−1) cgm-remote-monitor bf/food 73495331 1 BF-16, and BF-35 surfaced while fixing it cgm-remote-monitor bf/merge b06c6faf 1 BF-36 cgm-remote-monitor bf/parms eb0bc918 3 BF-37, BF-38, BF-39 cgm-remote-monitor bf/reads 2ecfeb53 6 six read-path fixes — BF-01, BF-05, BF-13, BF-14, BF-15, BF-33 nightscout-connect fix/connect-timer-jitter c1cce2a2 — T0.4 start jitter + BF-34

Plus, prepared locally in nightscout-connect: branch release/v0.0.14 and an annotated tag v0.0.14, both at 649a7de2.

The SHAs that moved, and why. bf/coercion 88d1f8a4 → ab197bf8 (9 files, code only; 40 CHANGELOG lines removed) → b7519fc7 (2026-09-16: two code comments and one paragraph of the commit message stated BF-32's refuted mechanism as fact) → f829ea11 (same day: BF-68, a regression the branch introduced — $type's operand is a BSON type code and excluding it from conversion turned a working find[sgv][$type]=2 into an HTTP 500). 29 passing. bf/reads 0d19bb31 → 2ecfeb53 (the changelog-only commit dropped, and the branch un-stacked from bf/coercion and rebased directly onto origin/dev, which is why it now carries 6 commits rather than 8). Safety refs bf/coercion.bak-changelog (88d1f8a4) and bf/reads.bak-changelog (0d19bb31) are kept until the PRs merge, as is the older bf/reads-prerebase (824380a0). Verified at the time of the strip: git range-diff shows all six bf/reads commits content-identical (=); bf/coercion differs from its backup by exactly the 40 changelog lines and no code; messages, authorship and dates preserved.

A third SHA moved, 2026-09-16, after this document was written. bf/auth 64db1f35 → 56ed29d2, and the branch now carries 3 commits rather than 2. The new commit removes a console.log('Loading', opts) from lib/authorization/storage.js — a per-request debug print of request-derived values, the same defect class as the count-path filter leak fixed on bf/reads. The line is not introduced by the branch; it is on origin/dev at storage.js:84, and it was taken here because it sits in a file this branch already rewrites. It was the last failing gate on queue item P0-C, which now reports 3/3 runnable gates passing. 64db1f35 still exists on the branch and is still the BF-17 commit, so references to it as the BF-17 commit elsewhere remain correct; only the tip and the commit count moved. The diff is still ten files.

origin/dev has not moved. Re-fetched live during this rewrite: origin/dev is a8888f0d, dated 2026-09-09, and git rev-list --count a8888f0d..origin/dev is 0. Every branch here shares that base and none of them is drifting from anything. (A cached FETCH_HEAD a day old is the stale-ref trap to avoid when re-checking this.)
